name: calorya
description: Cross-platform daily health & nutrition tracker — Next.js PWA + Expo, sharing one domain core.

scripts.build:web: npm run build:packages && npm run build -w @calorya/web

//overrides: Exactly one Metro, pinned to the version Expo SDK 57 ships.
Two packages ask for Metro and they do not agree:
That caret is the problem. Whether npm satisfies it with the 0.84.5 already
in the tree or fetches a newer 0.84.x depends on when the install ran and
which npm ran it, so two machines installing the SAME lockfile can end up
with different trees. When the newer one wins it gets hoisted to the root,
Expo's packages nest their own 0.84.5, and the build dies with
'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading transformFile)' — the CLI
loads Bundler from one copy and the transformer from the other.
Pinning every metro-* package removes the choice. Bump these together with
the Expo SDK, matching whatever @expo/metro depends on.
//overrides-worklets: react-native-worklets is a PEER dependency of react-native-reanimated@4,
not a normal one, so whether it gets installed at all is up to npm's peer
auto-install — it landed in one machine's tree and not another's. When it
is absent, babel-preset-expo still asks for 'react-native-worklets/plugin',
the transformer fails to construct, and Metro then reports the useless
'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading transformFile)' instead of
the real cause. apps/mobile depends on it explicitly now; this override
collapses the peer-installed copy onto the same version so the native
build has only one to autolink.
